primary_findings.title: WebSocket keeps pushing to a user disabled after handshake
primary_findings.why_it_matters:
T0-B's stated outcome is '停用立即生效' (deactivation takes effect immediately). For HTTP that holds because every request re-reads users.status. The notification WebSocket is a long-lived channel whose credential check happens exactly once, at handshake: a user who connects, is then disabled, keeps receiving every notification pushed to them until the socket closes — which is never on its own. So the account-status gate is effective on HTTP and ineffective on the one channel that keeps working after the account is switched off, and the docs claim a single global rule ('每请求查一次 users.status ⇒ 停用立即生效') without carving this out (app/services/user_status_service.py:22-24 states the guarantee unqualified).

Exposure today is limited: no frontend caller of /api/v1/ws/notifications was found in this repo, so the channel is not known to be in use. The gap is that the batch's own guarantee is stated without the exception.

primary_findings.why_it_matters:

primary_findings.title: Deployment assertion goes green while mock-login route is mounted
primary_findings.why_it_matters:
assert_mock_auth_not_exposed is a deployment guard whose stated invariant is 'the mock router must not be mounted in production'. The rewrite correctly replaced the app.routes walk (which FastAPI 0.141's lazy mounting made a no-op), but it swapped one proxy for another: it now asserts on the OpenAPI schema, which is a *derived view* of the routing table and is empty for any route excluded from the schema. A single plausible edit — including the mock router with include_in_schema=False so it stops showing up in /docs — makes the assertion pass while /auth/mock-login is mounted and reachable. The production double gate inside the endpoint still refuses to issue a token, so this is not a live bypass today; but the assertion that is supposed to fail fast on a mis-mounted router no longer fails, i.e. the guard this batch rewrote as a silent-pass fix is still a silent-pass.

Independently verified: the OpenAPI-path check is version-independent for this failure mode — include_router(..., include_in_schema=False) keeps the route out of `app.openapi()['paths']` on both FastAPI 0.135 and 0.141.1 — so the finding does not depend on the version question raised about the comment above it (pcs-backend/uv.lock pins fastapi 0.141.1; the system interpreter has 0.135.3).

primary_findings.title: Fail-closed lineage guard makes PSV lineage permanently 404
primary_findings.why_it_matters:
T0-D turned the lineage guard fail-closed: any record_type that is not in the guard registry now returns 404 instead of falling through. The registry is derived from RECORD_TYPE_REGISTRY, but that registry does not contain PsvResult — yet PsvResult is exactly one of the models that writes lineage rows (finalize_calc_record in psv_persist). Before this diff the guard skipped unregistered types, so GET /lineage/PsvResult/{id}/graph resolved the real lineage; after it, the same request is a hard 404 for every PSV record.

Independently verified in this repo: (a) `grep -n PsvResult app/services/calc_lineage.py` ⇒ 0 hits (the 21 registry keys are PipingResult, PumpResult, FlashResult, PipeNetworkResult, TwoPhaseResult, ReliefResult, ColumnSizingResult, MixerResult, ProjectCalculationStandardProfile, HeatResult, VesselResult, SepEquipResult, cv_result, restriction_result, flare_system_result, cooling_tower_result, psychro_result, OpenChannelResult, FiltrationResult, CostEstResult, ThermosiphonCirculationResult); (b) `app/services/psv/psv_persist.py:444` calls `finalize_calc_record` ⇒ `LineageTracker.track` writes `record_type=record.__class__.__name__` (app/services/lineage.py:109) ⇒ real `data_lineage` rows with record_type='PsvResult' exist; (c) PsvResult has `project_id` (declared_attr on RecordMixin, app/models/mixins.py) ⇒ it *could* be registered.

⇒ The derivation inherits a pre-existing gap in RECORD_TYPE_REGISTRY and turns it from 'works' into 'permanently unavailable'. The plan's own completeness step (T0-D Step 3.3) asks for a mirror test asserting 'every record_type LineageTracker.track can write is in the registry', but the implementation parameterizes over RECORD_TYPE_REGISTRY's keys ⇒ a model that writes lineage without being a registry member (PsvResult) can never be caught. primary_findings.title: 重试/提交已成功但列表刷新失败 ⇒ 报成「批量提交失败」
primary_findings.why_it_matters:
hook 的 submit() 把「提交请求」与「提交后的列表刷新（onDone）」放在同一个 try 里、共用一个 catch。onDone 一旦 reject（网络抖动、页面卸载、调用方自己的 load 未来改成会抛），catch 会 `setResult(null)`（把刚拿到的批次摘要弹窗关掉）并把异常 rethrow 给页面 ⇒ 页面顶部显示「批量提交校对失败」，而批次其实已经提交成功。用户据此重发整批 ⇒ 重复提交（后端会返回 already_in_approval 幂等提示，但用户先看到的是「失败」，且失败清单已被清空）。

这与 hook 自己的 docstring 明写的语义（「批次**整批**失败（网络 / 超限 / 403）⇒ **抛给调用方**」）和 catch 里的注释（「整批失败 ⇒ 没有新摘要」）不一致 —— 现在的实现把「刷新失败」也算成了「整批失败」。今天唯一消费者 StreamListPage 传的 onDone 是 load()，而 load 自己吞掉了所有异常 ⇒ 这条路径目前是潜伏的，不是活跃故障；但它是一颗装在失败路径上的地雷：下一次有人让 load 抛出（或者换一个消费者），错误文案会立刻开始撒谎。

discarded.title: Every authenticated request now pays a users.status DB round trip
discarded.reason: settled decision — plan T0-B Step 3 chose 方案 B (per-request users.status) and item E8 keeps 'status in the token claim' as a separate batch that only starts if the measured P95 exceeds the threshold; the candidate merely prefers another approach and the settled approach does achieve the agreed outcome. Its test-gap half (no perf-budget test for the probe) is kept under testing gaps.

residual_risks: Callsite completeness: every 'the only call site of current_actor is ws.py' / 'no other consumer of USER_DISABLED' statement in this round rests on text search over the tree (no symbol-level or AST search was available) ⇒ reflection, dependency_overrides, or dynamically registered call sites cannot be excluded.

Fail-open by construction on a missing users row: is_account_disabled queries User.user_id == <token user_id claim> and returns False when no row matches. A legacy account row whose user_id != uuid5(NAMESPACE_DNS, username) (the shape TODO-137 tracks) is invisible to the check ⇒ such a row stays fully accessible even when its status is DISABLED. The window is closed only by the repo's pre-release SQL check (SELECT count(*) FROM users WHERE user_id <> uuid5_derived(username)) = 0, which makes it a deployment precondition rather than a code defect; TODO-137 does not register it as a hole in the disable guarantee.

users.status is a free VARCHAR(20) with no CHECK constraint restricting it to ACTIVE/DISABLED (pcs-backend/app/models/project.py:157). is_account_disabled only compares against UserStatus.DISABLED.value, so a NULL status or a typo'd value reads as 'not disabled' (fail-open). No code path writes such a value today.

The mock-login double gate is only as strong as the two conditions it combines: is_production is an exact string compare (self.env == "production", pcs-backend/app/core/config.py:129) and the shipped pcs-backend/.env.example sets PCS_ENABLE_MOCK_LOGIN=true. A deployment that copies the example file and sets ENV to anything other than exactly 'production' (e.g. 'prod', 'Production') both mounts the mock router and passes the second gate ⇒ mock-login stays live and issues a SYSTEM_ADMIN token for 'dan'. The switch is also absent from docker-compose.yml and .github/workflows, so any deployment or CI environment that relies on mock login must add it explicitly.

The WebSocket handshake accepts the bearer token as a query parameter (?token=), which puts credentials into access logs and proxy logs (CWE-532). The token transport itself is unchanged by this diff and no frontend caller of /api/v1/ws/notifications was found in this repo, so live exposure could not be established.

reference_counts sends the whole project's stream ids as an IN list (pcs-backend/app/services/stream_service.py:378 and :393) while list_by_project has no LIMIT ⇒ one bind parameter per stream id per query, two queries per list request, and a per-request plan whose cost grows with the project rather than with the returned page. The IN list is also redundant with the project_id predicate that is already there (ids are a subset of the project's streams). Nothing is broken today; bundle the removal with the TODO-143 index work in P10-D rather than shipping it alone.

LineageTracker.by_source_ref (new in this diff, pcs-backend/app/services/lineage.py:144-176) filters on data_lineage(source_ref_type, source_ref_id) — neither column is indexed (pcs-backend/app/models/system.py:46-47) and the table only grows ⇒ every open of the stream lineage tab costs a scan plus a sort for 'ORDER BY occurred_at DESC, lineage_id DESC' (the LIMIT is applied in the database, so the response is bounded but the scan/sort is not). Same root cause as the recorded TODO-143 deferral; a composite (source_ref_type, source_ref_id, occurred_at DESC) is what makes it an early-terminating index scan — worth folding into the P10-D index task.

LineageTracker.by_source_ref filters only on source_ref_type/source_ref_id and carries no project_id predicate, while the sibling count column was just given one (Q7: only same-project references count). No code path was found that creates a cross-project reference today (create_outlet_stream forces source.project_id == project_id; flash_persist uses stream.project_id), so this is a consistency/hardening item rather than a demonstrated defect.

reference_count is a public field on StreamResponse but is only computed by the project stream list endpoint; GET/PATCH /streams/{id} answer 0 ⇒ '0' means both 'no references' and 'not computed'. The OpenAPI description ('下游物流数 + 闪蒸结果数') does not say the field is only populated by the list endpoint, so an external consumer reading the contract would trust a wrong number. (Registered as a known limitation in the batch context; the frontend only reads the field on the list page.)

CreateStreamRequest.workspace_id is now accepted and silently dropped (the endpoint forces project.workspace_id). The change is announced (OpenAPI deprecated:true + description) and the frontend never sends the field, but an external client that deliberately targeted another workspace receives no 409/422 telling it its value was ignored.

The frontend's SESSION_OVER_CODES set also lacks 'REFRESH_REVOKED', which the ADR-0046 §5 token_version gate can return from POST /auth/refresh — pre-existing (that path predates this batch) but the same shape as the USER_DISABLED gap in finding #1.

For record_type='streams', /upstream answers 200 + [] while /graph and /downstream answer data or 404 — the 'no upstream rows' vs 'not found' distinction is deliberate and documented in the endpoint docstrings, but the three endpoints still answer three different status/shape combinations for the same record family ⇒ a client must special-case streams.

The MSW lineage mock always returns a synthetic root (source 'MANUAL', change_summary '物流本身（合成根节点）') regardless of the requested record_type, while the backend returns a real lineage row (source 'CALC') for non-streams record types. The shape matches the contract (ajv-checked) but the semantics only match the backend for record_type='streams'.

current_actor's per-request users.status read propagates DB failures upward (not swallowed, not turned into 'user not found') ⇒ one DB blip returns 500 on every endpoint that Depends(current_actor). The direction is fail-closed (deny everyone rather than admit everyone), which matches the batch's intent, but there is no degradation signal of its own (no status cache, no breaker).

The WS handshake now shares fate with the DB (it was pure-CPU JWT decoding before): when the DB is unavailable or the pool is exhausted, a handshake waits out pool_timeout=30s before failing ⇒ a reconnect storm occupies 30s per handshake. The pool parameters themselves (pool_size=10 / max_overflow=20 / pool_timeout=30) are unchanged.

The per-request users.status probe is paid by every authenticated request, not only the 20 logistics endpoints this batch was about; the import-graph estimate of the blast radius is a lower bound because the graph does not track Depends()-based usage. The cost itself is a settled decision (plan T0-B Step 4 measured it against the P95 thresholds; plan item E8 keeps 'status in the token claim' as a separate batch that only starts if the measured P95 exceeds the threshold) ⇒ not re-raised as a finding here.

users.roles is overwritten only when a real login succeeds: if a person is removed from every mapped LDAP group, resolve_role raises LdapAuthError ⇒ the login fails ⇒ the overwrite never happens ⇒ users.roles keeps the old role ⇒ role-scoped notification selection (notification_recipients.resolve_role_recipients) still finds them. AD sync (ad_sync._apply, which overwrites and nulls the role when there is none) covers that scenario, so this depends on AD sync running (ADR-0046 registers 'role changes are not immediate' as a known boundary).

The reference-count 口径 (downstream streams + flash results) and the delete gate's 口径 (state points + flash results) are deliberately different and share no constant or assertion ⇒ changing one will not turn the other red (SPEC §7.7.1 documents the difference, but nothing pins it in code).

'reference_count' carries default: 0 in OpenAPI but is not in the required list ⇒ the frontend's ajv ratchet does not fail when a seed or mock omits it (ajv does not apply defaults); only tsc catches the drift today.

FastAPI version sensitivity: pcs-backend/uv.lock pins fastapi 0.141.1 while the system interpreter has 0.135.3 ⇒ assertions that depend on framework routing/schema behaviour are version-bound (main.py's comment about 'FastAPI ≥ 0.141 lazy mounting' describes the locked version, not the system one) ⇒ any such assertion should name the version it was verified against.

pcs-backend/app/api/v1/lineage.py's _stream_graph re-reads the stream with session.get(Stream, stream_id) although the guard already loaded that row; this is not an extra round trip (Session.get consults the identity map first), so the cost is only a redundant re-read plus an unused return contract — see finding #12.

assert_mock_auth_not_exposed calls app.openapi() at startup, which materialises the whole schema ⇒ a route whose response model cannot be introspected would abort startup rather than pass silently (the failure mode of this call at boot was not exercised by any test in the diff).

pcs-backend/app/services/stream_service.py's list_by_project has no LIMIT and the list endpoint returns the whole project ⇒ the per-request cost of the list endpoint grows with the project, not with a page; no bound is asserted anywhere (see the testing gaps).
The backend batch-submit path (POST /streams/batch-submit) does not appear in the diff hunks ⇒ it was treated as pre-existing and its per-item work was not reviewed in depth in this round.

.wolf/anatomy-index.json still records pcs-backend/app/services/token_issuer.py's symbol as _merge_real_role while the final code renamed it to _write_real_role ⇒ the OpenWolf index lags the last rename; the file is hook-maintained and must not be hand-edited, so this is a note only.
testing_gaps: No frontend test covers '401 USER_DISABLED ⇒ clearSession + redirect to /login', and SESSION_OVER_CODES has no table-driven test at all ⇒ changing the whitelist has no guard rail (the missing scenario behind finding #1).

SESSION_OVER_CODES is a hand-written second source of truth for session-ending 401 codes ⇒ any new backend 'session is over' code (USER_DISABLED, USER_LOGIN_DENIED_DISABLED, …) will not be recognised by the client ⇒ worth an architecture test (backend error-code table ↔ frontend set) or a shared 'session codes' contract.

No test pins that /graph and /downstream behave identically for record_type='streams' (same max_depth ⇒ same downstream row cap, both 'newest first') — SPEC requires the two endpoints to agree, but no assertion compares them on the same data_lineage rows.

No HTTP-level case covers a record type that really writes lineage rows but is absent from RECORD_TYPE_REGISTRY (PsvResult today): the mirror test compares against RECORD_TYPE_REGISTRY, while app/services/calc_lineage.py's own docstring states that the registry is not the supported set of finalize_calc_record (duck typing, TODO-048) ⇒ the test name overstates what it proves (this is the coverage gap behind finding #8).

No end-to-end case covers 'cross-project reference ⇒ reference_count is 0 in the list response': the service layer has two cross-project exclusion cases, but the endpoint only asserts that project_id is passed through ⇒ if the endpoint passed the wrong project id, or the service's project_id predicate were dropped, nothing would go red end to end.

No query-count assertion pins the round-trip count of GET /projects/{project_id}/streams (4 before this batch → 6 now) ⇒ a future change that turns the two aggregates into a per-row query would stay green.

No perf-budget test covers the per-request users.status probe. The repo already has the pattern (tests/services/test_export_service.py has a perf budget) ⇒ a request-count or latency budget for the list endpoint would give the plan's P95 threshold (item E8: >5ms ⇒ evaluate 'status in the token claim') an automatic gate instead of a one-off measurement.

reference_counts is never exercised with a large id list (the unit tests use a handful of streams) ⇒ a case with a few thousand ids, asserting both the returned counts and the parameter count / query shape, would make the O(project) parameter growth visible before it matters.

No test asserts that by_source_ref's limit is applied in the database (as opposed to truncating after fetch) ⇒ a statement-capturing test would pin the 'bounded response AND bounded scan' property the endpoint docstring claims.

No test asserts that a field added to _serialize survives the LineageGraphResponse response model: the existing 'synthetic root has the same shape as a real root' test compares _serialize's dict to _serialize's dict, not to the validated response body ⇒ a schema/serializer drift would pass it.

No backend test asserts that the three lineage endpoints return the same representation for the same row (e.g. the /graph node body against the /downstream node body for the same lineage_id, including the occurred_at string form) ⇒ the '+00:00' vs 'Z' divergence behind finding #4 has no guard.

No case covers current_actor's DB read failing (connection lost / pool timeout / statement timeout) ⇒ the behaviour the rest of the system depends on ('DB blip ⇒ 500 everywhere, fail-closed') is pinned by no test; tests/api/v1/test_user_disabled_guard.py only covers DISABLED / ACTIVE / no users row / awaitable / endpoint still usable.

No case covers the disabled check against a users row whose user_id is not the derived uuid5(NAMESPACE_DNS, username) (the TODO-137 legacy shape), nor against a NULL or unrecognised status value ⇒ both currently evaluate to 'not disabled' and nothing records that as intentional.

T0-E only covers the 'row already exists' cases (append / overwrite / repeated login does not append) plus 'mock never writes' ⇒ no case covers 'real login whose role was downgraded to empty' (role is None), where _write_real_role writes roles=[role] while the AD-sync side writes roles=[role] if role else None — the two sides disagree at that boundary.

GET /streams/{id} (single stream) always answers reference_count = 0 (registered as a known limitation) ⇒ no case pins that 'always 0'; the frontend only reads the field on the list page, so a future detail page would silently show a wrong number.

No frontend case pins that the synthetic root and a real root expose the same field set: the backend has test_synthetic_root_has_same_shape_as_real_root (same keys), but the frontend's buildLineageGraph mock is only ajv-checked against the contract shape ⇒ the two can drift apart without either side going red.
No case covers a WebSocket that stays open across a user-disable event (status re-check on the delivery path) — the scenario behind finding #5's open decision.

The mock-login gate tests cover the PCS_ENABLE_MOCK_LOGIN env-var name and the production RuntimeError, but there is no test that the startup assertion trips when the mock router is mounted with include_in_schema=False (the exact green-while-red case of finding #7), nor that the lifespan actually runs the assertion in a production-configured app.

The N+1 guard in tests/api/v1/test_deliverables_current_version.py identifies the actor layer's users.status query by substring ('users' in s and 'status' in s) ⇒ any business query that mentions both the users table and a status column would be miscounted (false red) and would also be dropped from the ≤3 business-query budget ⇒ the criterion should test the compiled statement's table/column names instead of the raw SQL text.

The MSW batch-submit mock always answers failed: [] ⇒ the persistent failure bar and the '只重试失败项' path — the batch's headline UX deliverable — can never be rendered in the browser-QA lane ⇒ a green browser regression says nothing about T1.

The negative lineage-tab case waits on a real 300ms sleep and asserts the tooltip text is absent ⇒ it only proves the tooltip did not appear within that window (a slow machine would still pass) ⇒ use fake timers and assert the tooltip node does not exist.
